name: Waterways Leisure Tourism Ltd
title: Waterways Leisure Tourism Ltd - 544802 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: Single-ship cruise operator where Q1 FY27 profit was hit by fuel costs (~Rs14 Cr EBITDA hit), with capacity doubling via Cordelia Sky in Sept-Oct 2026; no supply discipline signals, pricing recovery deferred to Q3.

utilisation.quote: we report a load factor of 105% for Q1 with an increase of 4.3% of average ticket price versus Q1 2025

summary.headline: Q1 FY27 net profit Rs.22.77 Crores (~12% margin) on 105% load factor, with fuel costs the main EBITDA drag.
summary.overview: Management attributed the quarter to a Middle East-driven spike in fuel prices, which took roughly Rs.14 crores out of EBITDA, while load factor rose to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4.3% year on year. Guests served exceeded 55,700 and staterooms booked reached 24,245, up about 10%. Management expects fuel surcharges on new bookings to show up from end-Q2/early-Q3, and says the second ship (Cordelia Sky) brings a much higher suite count. Finance cost roughly doubled to about Rs.4 crores on a bank loan taken to support rating and FD-backed arrangements.

segments.name: Empress (existing ship)
segments.commentary: Revenue growth for June 2026 vs June 2025 estimated at about 8-9% by management; expected to move to 10-12% going forward. Empress has about 69 suite and balcony cabins and about 800 total cabins.

segments.name: Cordelia Sky (new ship)
segments.commentary: Expected to have about 269 suite and balcony cabins and about 1,000 total cabins, with nine restaurants versus three on Empress. Management says revenue potential per ship is almost 100% higher than the current vessel.

guidance_outlook: Management expects a year of revenue and earnings growth, driven by cruise brand preference and new destinations.
Fuel surcharges on new bookings expected to recover most of the extra fuel cost, with impact visible from end-Q2 / beginning of Q3.
Management is hopeful that the extra fuel cost will be offset by year-end through additional savings, as fuel prices move toward forecast levels.
Management says it is planning on an annual-average basis rather than quarterly, and Q2 is being used as a lower-capacity test period for new itineraries without affecting annual results.
Cost sharing across three ships (fixed shore-side marketing and management fees) expected to lower per-ship cost once the fleet is fully operational.
capex_capacity: Cordelia Sky: ship sails from September 19, 2026; handover September 25, 2026; arrives Mumbai October 15, 2026; maiden voyage October 23, 2026.
Cordelia Sun to follow Sky; the company says both ships are available for booking since April 2025.
Two new Lakshadweep islands being added; new West Coast ports and destinations under test.
Four more international sailings from the West Coast during monsoon 2027; Maldives and Colombo sailings on East Coast from October 2026.
New direct sales centre in Cochin to open in September 2026; loyalty programme Chairman's Club to roll out by end-Q2.
demand_pricing: Advance bookings of Rs.65 crores currently, which management says translates to about Rs.110-115 crores of revenue for the shorter sailings.
Highlight sailings including the maiden voyage, Christmas, New Year and Holi are already booked, with corporate demand also reported.
Management says ticket prices do not change much; revenue growth is driven by cabin mix, not pricing.
Fuel price: VLSFO average was $580 per metric tonne over last year, peaked at $1,228 when tensions started, and is about $800 currently per management.
Port charges abroad said to be lower than in India due to GST on domestic port charges; more sea days on international cruises reduce port cost impact.

qa_highlights.question: Why has EBITDA margin declined over the last two quarters, and is it one-off?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main driver is fuel, worth about Rs.14 crores; crew wage increases of about Rs.2 crores (about 16% in percentage terms) and food costs of about Rs.1 crore were smaller items.

qa_highlights.question: How will higher fuel costs be passed on to customers given advance bookings?
qa_highlights.answer: Fuel surcharges apply to new bookings only, not already-sold Q1 cruises, so recovery shows from end-Q2/beginning-Q3. Fuel was pre-ordered and bought at prices that management says have fallen from the peak.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 revenue growth from occupancy or ticket price?
qa_highlights.answer: Both: load factor rose from 99.9% to 105% and average ticket price rose about 4%.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost roughly double?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said a loan was taken from IDFC First Bank, backed by FDs, to support rating requirements; it carries a 1% prepayment cost and is being carried over, with the company citing zero net debt given matching FD assets.

qa_highlights.question: Expected Q2 top-line run rate versus about Rs.190 crores in Q1, and like-for-like Empress growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a numeric Q2 run rate, pointing to cabin mix. Empress growth was about 8-9% in the quarter, expected to reach 10-12%.

qa_highlights.question: Strategy to expand margins beyond fuel?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said fixed shore-side marketing, management fees and other costs will be spread across three ships as the fleet grows, with better purchasing power.

risks_watch: Fuel price volatility tied to Middle East tensions; the company says prices have recovered to around $800/MT from the $1,228 peak but tensions have restarted.
Fuel surcharge recovery only applies to new bookings, so margin benefit is delayed to Q3 and depends on booking pace.
Cordelia Sky delivery timeline (handover September 25, 2026) and maiden voyage on October 23, 2026.
Management declined to give a forward statement on how fast the second ship will reach full utilisation.
Finance cost and loan structure: IDFC First Bank loan with 1% prepayment cost; rating upgrade cited as the reason for it.
Crew wage increases (about 16% in percentage terms) may persist into future quarters.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, bookings and fleet expansion, with specific dates and numbers. More cautious and evasive on forward numbers: declined to give a Q2 revenue run rate and to forecast ramp-up of the second ship, and framed the margin recovery as dependent on fuel prices and booking timing.
key_quotes: Despite these industry wide impacts and headwinds, we report a load factor of 105% for Q1 with an increase of 4.3% of average ticket price versus Q1 2025.
What drives the revenue is not the pricing it is the cabin mix.
So the results of these extra charges will actually show end of Q2, beginning of Q3.

adds.what: Cordelia Sky second ship, ~269 suite/balcony cabins and ~1,000 total cabins (about double capacity per management)
Two new Lakshadweep islands added to itineraries
Four more international sailings from West Coast during monsoon 2027
New direct sales centre in Cochin opening September 2026

growth.why: Management guides a year of revenue and earnings growth and Empress revenue growth of 10-12% going forward (8-9% in Q1), backed by the Cordelia Sky launch (sailing Sept 2026, ~Rs.65 Cr advance bookings worth Rs.110-115 Cr revenue) and 105% load factor, though fuel costs (~Rs.14 Cr EBITDA hit) and an unquantified fuel-surcharge recovery leave earnings timing uncertain.
